snapshot.title: Forensic Analysis: Firmware 2.4.11a Root Cause

lines.msg: Loading firmware image: UAS-02-FW-2.4.11a (SHA-256: d4e9a1f7b2c8e6d1a3f4b5c6e7f8a9b0c1d2e3f4g5h6i7j8k9l0m)
Control authority transfer logic: disabled in profile 2.3.1 (parameter: 'failover_logic = OFF')
Link loss detected at 08:55:12 (2.4 GHz); attempting re-establishment via unapproved protocol (RTP-07X) not in HUOG-FOM-1 Annex B
UAS-02 entered stalled state: no failover to 461.0375 MHz; attempting to re-authenticate via rogue channel (915 MHz band, unencrypted)
GPS-071 spoofing event detected at 08:58:14 — 4.3 ms signal jitter, position jump from 178 ft AGL to 420 ft AGL
Class C airspace boundary crossed at 08:58:18 (1.1 km WNW of Horton Field), 400 ft AGL

Firmware 2.4.11a introduced a bug in control authority transfer: failed to trigger RTL or fallback to backup link; instead, initiated unapproved protocol (RTP-07X) causing climb into controlled airspace
OEM fleet portal shows no geofence unlock or firmware push from Group; update was not approved via HUOG-FOM-1 or HUOG-ISP-2026
Parameter change log: 'failover_logic = OFF' was not manually set; appears in 2.3.1 profile imported from HUOG-FOM-1 v1.3 (2026-09-01)
Root cause confirmed: firmware 2.4.11a contains unpatched bug in control authority transfer logic. The 2.3.1 profile (used in pre-flight) disables failover; update did not correct it.

snapshot.instructorNote: This inject confirms the root cause of the flyaway. The team must now decide whether to resume operations under risk thresholds, knowing the firmware bug is not patched.
